title: Technical Graphics at Royal Crest: Every building starts as a line
_note: say = text sent to ElevenLabs (numbers spelled out where they must be read a certain way); cap = on-screen caption. TIN uses ElevenLabs' premade voice 'George'; swap voice_id for any voice in your account.

lines.say: Every building in Zimbabwe started the same way.
lines.cap: Every building in Zimbabwe started the same way.

lines.say: With bricks?
lines.cap: With bricks?

lines.say: With a line. One pencil line, on a drawing board.
lines.cap: With a line. One pencil line, on a drawing board.

lines.say: Wait. Did you hear that? Every building starts as a line.
lines.cap: Wait. Did you hear that? Every building starts as a line.

lines.say: Welcome to the drawing room at Royal Crest Academy, in Bikita. Today: Technical Graphics, from the first line to a full 3D model.
lines.cap: Welcome to the drawing room at Royal Crest Academy, in Bikita. Today: Technical Graphics, from the first line to a full 3D model.

lines.say: Lesson one. The tools. A drawing board, a T-square, set squares at forty-five and thirty-sixty degrees, and a compass.
lines.cap: Lesson one: the tools. A drawing board, a T-square, set squares at 45° and 30/60°, and a compass.

lines.say: That's the compass from the opening shot!
lines.cap: That’s the compass from the opening shot!

lines.say: And lines have a language. Thick for outlines. Thin for construction. Dashed for hidden edges. Chain lines for centres.
lines.cap: And lines have a language. Thick for outlines. Thin for construction. Dashed for hidden edges. Chain lines for centres.

lines.say: So a drawing is a sentence, written in lines.
lines.cap: So a drawing is a sentence, written in lines.

lines.say: Lesson two. Isometric drawing. Lines at thirty degrees, so one drawing shows three faces at once.
lines.cap: Lesson two: isometric drawing. Lines at 30°, so one drawing shows three faces at once.

lines.say: Wait, that cube just became a house!
lines.cap: Wait, that cube just became a house!

lines.say: Box it first, then cut it. That's how engineers think.
lines.cap: Box it first, then cut it. That’s how engineers think.

lines.say: Lesson three. Orthographic projection. We put the house inside an imaginary glass box.
lines.cap: Lesson three: orthographic projection. We put the house inside an imaginary glass box.

lines.say: A glass box?
lines.cap: A glass box?

lines.say: Then we flatten each side. Front view. End view. Plan. Projection lines carry every edge across, so the views line up exactly.
lines.cap: Then we flatten each side. Front view. End view. Plan. Projection lines carry every edge across, so the views line up exactly.

lines.say: So a builder can read every size from three flat drawings. Brilliant.
lines.cap: So a builder can read every size from three flat drawings. Brilliant.

lines.say: Lesson four. Perspective: how the eye really sees. Width and depth lines run to two vanishing points on the horizon.
lines.cap: Lesson four: perspective, how the eye really sees. Width and depth lines run to two vanishing points on the horizon.

lines.say: Two points. So where's the third?
lines.cap: Two points. So where’s the third?

lines.say: Look up at a tall building. The vertical lines lean together, and meet at a third point, high in the sky.
lines.cap: Look up at a tall building. The vertical lines lean together, and meet at a third point, high in the sky.

lines.say: Wait, that's the Burj Khalifa! The tallest building in the world.
lines.cap: Wait, that’s the Burj Khalifa! The tallest building in the world.

lines.say: And it started as lines on a drawing. Look down from the top, and the third point drops below you. That is three-point perspective.
lines.cap: And it started as lines on a drawing. Look down from the top, and the third point drops below you. That is three-point perspective.

lines.say: Lesson five. Sections. A cutting plane slices the building. We hatch the cut, and add dimensions in millimetres.
lines.cap: Lesson five: sections. A cutting plane slices the building. We hatch the cut, and add dimensions in millimetres.

lines.say: So you can see inside a wall, without breaking it.
lines.cap: So you can see inside a wall, without breaking it.

lines.say: Okay. But drawing boards, in twenty twenty-seven?
lines.cap: Okay. But drawing boards, in 2027?

lines.say: Here's the twist. Every skill on the board leads to BIM: Building Information Modelling.
lines.cap: Here’s the twist. Every skill on the board leads to BIM: Building Information Modelling.

lines.say: Now the model comes first. Every wall, slab and pipe knows what it is, what it's made of, and how much of it there is.
lines.cap: Now the model comes first. Every wall, slab and pipe knows what it is, what it’s made of, and how much of it there is.

lines.say: Wait. Did that model just count its own concrete?
lines.cap: Wait. Did that model just count its own concrete?

lines.say: Thirty-five cubic metres, for one floor, straight from the model. Then the services: hot water, cold water, waste and air, all checked before anyone digs.
lines.cap: 35 m³ for one floor, straight from the model. Then the services: hot water, cold water, waste and air, all checked before anyone digs.

lines.say: And then you build it. Layer by layer.
lines.cap: And then you build it. Layer by layer.

lines.say: So what does this mean for a child from Bikita?
lines.cap: So what does this mean for a child from Bikita?

lines.say: A profession. Architect. Civil and structural engineer. Quantity surveyor. Draughtsperson and CAD technician. Town planner. BIM coordinator.
lines.cap: A profession. Architect. Civil and structural engineer. Quantity surveyor. Draughtsperson and CAD technician. Town planner. BIM coordinator.

lines.say: Zimbabwe is building. Roads, homes, schools, mines, and dams like Tokwe-Mukosi, right here in Masvingo province.
lines.cap: Zimbabwe is building. Roads, homes, schools, mines, and dams like Tokwe-Mukosi, right here in Masvingo province.

lines.say: Every one of those projects needs people who can read and draw the plans. Professionals who can work here at home, or anywhere in the world.
lines.cap: Every one of those projects needs people who can read and draw the plans. Professionals who can work here at home, or anywhere in the world.

lines.say: At Royal Crest, it starts in Form One. Technical Graphics on real drawing boards, alongside Building, Wood and Metal Technology, and Computer Science.
lines.cap: At Royal Crest, it starts in Form 1. Technical Graphics on real drawing boards, alongside Building, Wood and Metal Technology, and Computer Science.

lines.say: Science. Innovation. Skill. Taught for ZIMSEC and Cambridge.
lines.cap: Science. Innovation. Skill. Taught for ZIMSEC and Cambridge.

lines.say: Parents: Form One places for January twenty twenty-seven are limited.
lines.cap: Parents: Form 1 places for January 2027 are limited.

lines.say: Come and see the drawing room for yourself.
lines.cap: Come and see the drawing room for yourself.

lines.say: Royal Crest Academy, Bikita. Call or WhatsApp zero seven one four, four zero four, zero nine zero.
lines.cap: Royal Crest Academy, Bikita. Call or WhatsApp 0714 404 090.

lines.say: Pick up a pencil. Draw your future.
lines.cap: Pick up a pencil. Draw your future.
